title: 1945: bare numbers
text: You begin where software began: binary instructions fed to a processor, one machine at a time.

title: 1957: the compiler
text: Grace Hopper and John Backus prove a program can translate readable code into fast machine code. Programming stops being wiring.

title: 1972: C and Unix
text: Dennis Ritchie's C and the Unix system written in it become the template for almost everything that follows.

title: 1974: SQL
text: Databases get a question language. You describe the answer you want and the system works out how.

title: 2005: Git
text: Linus Torvalds writes a distributed version control system in weeks. It becomes the universal standard.

title: Package managers
text: One command now pulls in hundreds of libraries. It is the magic of modern programming, and its biggest risk.

title: 2006: the cloud
text: Amazon rents computers by the hour. Containers and Kubernetes follow, and servers become software.

title: Now: AI writes code
text: Language models write, review and repair code. You wake up in the middle of that change.
